text:
jess-support: Escalation from Maya (customer) — dedicated VPC. After TLS termination at the NLB our service intermittently returns 403s. Customer says the same token works if they hit the instance directly, but hitting through the NLB -> HAProxy path sometimes strips the Authorization header. Repro steps + traces below.

maya-customer: seeing 403 on POST /v1/generate. Token valid in our IDP, we rotated it to be sure. Works for a bit, then 403s for ~30s, then 200 again. Happening multiple times per hour.

jess-support: Repro I did from their VPC (via customer VPN):
```
# hits NLB (TLS offload) -> our HAProxy sidecar -> app:8080
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://nlb-cust.example.com/v1/generate -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n"
# result: sometimes 403, sometimes 200
```
Captured headers at different hops:
- tcpdump at host before haproxy: Authorization present
- haproxy logs: backend request shows no Authorization header header name
- app log: "missing Authorization header -> 403"

omar-eng-infra: curious. Do you have the HAProxy config (bind line + http settings)? NLB is TLS-terminating, right? Any proxy-protocol enabled?

jess-support: NLB terminates TLS yes. HAProxy config snippet from customer host: 
```
global
  tune.bufsize 8192
defaults
  mode http
  option httplog
  timeout client 30s
frontend https-in
  bind *:80
  default_backend app-backend
backend app-backend
  server app1 127.0.0.1:8080 check
```
They said they don't have accept-proxy on bind because NLB wasn't sending proxy proto.

liam-eng-runtime: 8192 bufsize is small if the Authorization header or other headers get large (signed cookies, SSO assertions). HAProxy can drop or rewrite headers when buffer limits hit. Also some LBs (esp older ASN-based NLBs) can fragment headers across TCP segments which interacts poorly with sidecar proxies. Try increase tune.bufsize and tune.maxrewrite.

omar-eng-infra: +1. Also check for HTTP/2->HTTP/1 conversion at TLS offload: long header fields can be sent in CONTINUATION frames and sidecars might mishandle. Two quick checks: 1) enable PROXY v2 between NLB and HAProxy (so bind ... accept-proxy) and 2) increase tune.bufsize to 16384 and tune.maxrewrite to 16384, restart HAProxy.

sasha-eng-platform: Another angle: if Istio (or other ext_authz) is present upstream of the app, ext_authz filters sometimes normalize header names and can drop Authorization if a rule rewrites or expects a different header. Can you paste envoy/istio ext_authz policy?

jess-support: Customer says they have a lightweight istio sidecar but ext_authz is disabled. They do have an internal LUA header rewrite in HAProxy for session cookies. Sharing that snippet: 
```
http-request del-header X-Session-Debug
# some lua rewrite that copies cookie -> header if present
```
They also had an older haproxy version (2.0).

liam-eng-runtime: Older HAProxy + small bufsize + LUA rewrites == plausible root cause. LUA code that copies cookie into a header can trigger header size/rewrites and accidentally drop Authorization if buffers overflow or if header rewrite logic overwrites the header map.

maya-customer: any quick workaround we can ask them to apply? They need traffic stable during business hours.

omar-eng-infra: Quick workaround ideas:
- Add a header-preserve step: in HAProxy before any rewrite add `http-request set-header X-RW-AUTH %[req.hdr(Authorization)]` so the app can fallback to X-RW-AUTH if Authorization disappears.
- Increase tune.bufsize and tune.maxrewrite to 16384, upgrade HAProxy to 2.4+ where header handling is improved.
- If possible, configure the NLB to speak PROXY protocol v2 and enable `bind *:80 accept-proxy` on HAProxy so client connection metadata is preserved without TLS re-encoding.

jess-support: Example minimal change to try immediately (non-disruptive): add to frontend before rewrites:
```
http-request set-header X-RW-AUTH %[req.hdr(authorization)] if { req.hdr(authorization) -m found }
```
Then modify the app to check X-RW-AUTH for now (we can patch quickly).

liam-eng-runtime: If they cannot change app, another HAProxy tweak is `http-request replace-header Authorization .* "%-"` no that's risky. Prefer the X-RW-AUTH copy approach. Also increase buffer config and schedule an HAProxy restart out-of-hours.

bot-deploy: deployment note: if we push a platform sidecar change, ensure config change is rolled with canary across 10% of hosts to monitor for header regressions.

omar-eng-infra: After customer applied X-RW-AUTH copy + tune.bufsize=16384 on a small canary pool they reported no 403s for ~8h. We'll coordinate a staged rollout and HAProxy upgrade. Root cause hypothesis: HAProxy 2.0 buffer/rewrite bug interacting with header fragmentation from NLB TLS offload + custom LUA rewrites.

jess-support: Assigned to eng-infra (omar) to run canary + full upgrade. Leaving repro steps in case anyone needs to reproduce:
1) NLB TLS offload -> HAProxy 2.0 sidecar -> app
2) traffic with large cookies + Authorization header (try 3KB Authorization header or add long X-Claims header)
3) observe haproxy logs -> backend request missing Authorization -> app 403

sasha-eng-platform: also add a monitoring check: percent of 403s where request contains X-RW-AUTH vs Authorization to verify copy effectiveness.

jess-support: Thanks team — I'll update the customer.
